description: Add Owner-only/Allowlist/Anyone channel access policies to Slack Connections, a Manage-access control surface, and channel-originated stop/cancel authority.

tasks.title: Access-policy model, allowlist storage, and the single Owner-only access decision
tasks.spec: specs/channel-access-policy/spec.md#The Connection carries one access policy that decides who may invoke the Agent in a channel
tasks.description: Introduce the access-policy data model and consolidate the six inlined Owner-only checks into one access-decision service. Add an AccessPolicy field (default owner_only) and an allowlist child table to AgentConnection, then route every channel mention, bound-thread reply, and DM through a single SlackConnectionAccessDecider that evaluates the Owner-only/DM-Owner-only rule with no caching. This is a behavior-preserving substrate: after it, the system behaves exactly as before but through one decision point with the policy model in place.
acceptanceCriteria: AgentConnection gains an AccessPolicy field with kind constants and a column default of owner_only, threaded through CreateAsync, UpdateAsync (as a non-immutable field, not in ImmutableBindingFields), and ToRow/ToDomain; an additive EF migration creates the column so existing connections resolve to owner_only.

A new SlackConnectionAllowedMemberStore with its row, DbSet, and a unique index on (ProjectId, ConnectionId, SlackUserId) is registered, implements IAgentConnectionProviderCleanup with an ExecuteDeleteAsync filtered by (projectId, connectionId), and is added as the matching forward-registration in MohistServiceRegistration so allowed-member rows cascade-delete with the Connection.

A SlackConnectionAccessDecider (IScopedService) exposes EvaluateAsync(connection, senderSlackUserId, workspaceTeamId, conversationId, isDirectMessage) returning an AccessDecision, and the five channel owner-check sites in SlackConnectionRoutes plus the DM gate in SlackOwnerClaimService route through it instead of inlining sender == OwnerSlackUserId.

For owner_only and for any direct message, the decider authorizes only the Owner, reads no Slack API, and caches nothing; a non-Owner channel mention or bound-thread reply is rejected with an actionable reason and creates no AgentJob, AgentSession, SessionInput, or inbox entry.
The Owner is always authorized under owner_only, and the allowlist child table exists and is queryable even though the owner_only path does not depend on it.
Existing channel root-mention launch, thread follow-up, multi-Agent attribution, ambiguous-prompt, and DM behavior remain unchanged with the default owner_only policy applied through the decider.

Server spec tests cover owner_only accept, non-Owner reject with no resources created, DM remaining Owner-only, and the default owner_only policy on a newly created Connection; `npm test` passes with TreatWarningsAsErrors as lint and no real Slack, network, process, or wall-clock dependencies.
tasks.output: Access-policy storage, an allowlist child store with Connection-delete cascade, and a single Owner-only/DM-Owner-only access decision replacing the duplicated checks.
tasks.notes: Implements design D1 (storage) and D2 (single decider, owner_only + DM branches, no cache). The Owner is never stored in the allowlist child table, so 'Owner always present and immovable' is structural. Allowlist/Anyone decision rules and the Manage-access surface land in T-002 and T-003.

tasks.title: Allowlist and Anyone channel invocation authorization with live member validation
tasks.spec: specs/channel-access-policy/spec.md#Allowlist authorization is by stable workspace identity
tasks.description: Extend the access decider with the allowlist and anyone rules, proving current member status and channel visibility live from Slack on each non-Owner invocation. Under allowlist the sender must be the Owner or a listed member who is still a current regular workspace member; under anyone the sender must be a current regular workspace member in a channel where the Bot is a member. Because the decider never caches, policy and allowlist changes take effect on the next received input, including follow-ups on existing sessions, without revoking already-accepted work.
acceptanceCriteria: Under allowlist the decider authorizes the Owner, or a sender whose stable Slack identity is in the allowlist child table and who is confirmed a current regular member of the install workspace via UsersInfoAsync and SlackOwnerClaimService.IsEligibleMember (rejecting bot, deleted, guest, restricted, ultra-restricted, and other-team members).

Under anyone the decider additionally calls ConversationsInfoAsync and requires Channel.IsMember == true, so a sender in a channel the Bot is not a member of, a Slack Connect external participant, a guest, and any identity that cannot be confirmed are not authorized.

A Slack API call that returns not-OK, throws, or otherwise cannot confirm the member or channel-membership fact results in a deny decision, so an unverifiable identity never triggers the Agent; the Owner remains invokable because the Owner check needs no API call.

Tightening the policy (e.g. allowlist to owner_only) or removing an allowlist member causes the next received input, including a follow-up on an existing session, to be rejected immediately, while already-accepted work on that session is not revoked or interrupted and history is not deleted.
Loosening the policy (e.g. owner_only to allowlist) or adding a member accepts the next input without a process restart or reconnection.

A listed member who has since become a guest, been deleted, or been restricted is rejected, and a different member who merely shares a display name is evaluated solely on their own stable identity and is not authorized by the name match.

Server spec tests extend the RecordingSlackApiClient fake with settable per-user UsersInfo responses and a settable ConversationsInfo response, and cover allowlist listed-member accept, unlisted-member reject, Owner-always-accept, downgraded-listed-member reject, anyone workspace-member accept, external/guest/bot reject, bot-not-in-channel reject, DM remaining Owner-only under allowlist and anyone, immediate-effect tightening and loosening, no-name-auto-succession, and no-resource-creation on deny; `npm test` passes using fake Slack and injectable time only.
tasks.output: Allowlist and Anyone invocation authorization with live member and channel-visibility validation, immediate policy effect, and member-invalidation behavior.
tasks.notes: Implements design D2 (allowlist/anyone branches) and D3 (users.info + conversations.info live validation with safe-deny). Reuses the existing IsEligibleMember predicate so 'regular workspace member' semantics stay identical across claim, diagnostic, and access paths. Tested via seeded policy and allowlist rows; the owner-facing configuration surface is T-003.

tasks.title: Manage-access control surface: server endpoint, CLI, and Web
tasks.spec: specs/connection-access-management/spec.md#Only the Owner may change the access policy and allowlist
tasks.description: Make the access policies owner-configurable end-to-end. Add a POST manage-access endpoint that validates each proposed member against Slack and atomically replaces the policy and allowlist, return the Anyone execution-grant disclosure as a contract field, and wire the CLI flags and Web Connection panel to it so the Owner can select a policy, edit the allowlist by recognizable member information, and see the Anyone warning before it takes effect.
acceptanceCriteria: A POST /api/projects/{projectRef}/slack-connections/{id}/manage-access endpoint, project-resolved with no adapter credential like other management routes, accepts { accessPolicy, allowMembers } and rejects, before any mutation, an allowMembers list supplied with owner_only or anyone, and any member who is a bot, guest, deleted, restricted, or belongs to another workspace (validated via UsersInfoAsync and IsEligibleMember).

On success the endpoint updates the AccessPolicy column and replaces the allowlist child rows (delete existing, insert the new set) in one DbContext transaction, never stores the Owner as a removable row, and returns the updated connection read model including accessPolicy, allowMembers, and an anyoneDisclosure contract field.
Only an explicit Manage-access operation mutates the policy or allowlist; a Slack message does not change either, and a Slack member identity is not treated as a Mohist administrator identity.

The CLI connection edit command accepts --access-policy and a repeatable --allow-member, routes them to the manage-access endpoint (separate from the bot-name/avatar-hash PATCH), renders the anyoneDisclosure and requires confirmation before sending anyone, and errors before the call when --allow-member is supplied with owner_only or anyone.

The Web Connection panel renders the current policy, an allowlist editor backed by member name-and-avatar search that resolves to stable Slack identities, and the Anyone disclosure; display name and avatar are presentation only and are never the authorization identity.

Server spec tests cover setting each of the three policies, whole-list replace, the owner_only/anyone-with-allowMembers incompatibility rejection, invalid-member rejection, Owner auto-inclusion and non-storage, Owner-immovability, and the disclosure field; CLI and Web tests cover flag routing, the confirmation gate, and member-search-to-stable-id resolution.

End-to-end verification: after the Owner sets an allowlist via the endpoint a listed member's invocation is accepted, and after the Owner removes that member the member's next input is rejected; `npm test`, `npm run typecheck -w packages/web`, and `npm run test:ci -w packages/web` pass.
tasks.output: A usable Manage-access control surface across server API, CLI, and Web that lets the Owner select and change the policy and allowlist with member validation and the Anyone disclosure.
tasks.notes: Implements design D4 (validate-then-replace endpoint) and D6 (CLI flags + Web panel). The Anyone disclosure is a documented client-enforced contract field returned by the server; a server-side confirmation token is deferred (see design Open Questions). The endpoint reuses the IsEligibleMember predicate for add-time validation, matching the invocation-time check in T-002.

tasks.title: Channel-originated stop and cancel with Owner-or-initiator authority
tasks.spec: specs/channel-session-stop/spec.md#A channel-originated stop or cancel is permitted only to the Owner or the session initiator
tasks.description: Add a stop/cancel branch to the channel ingress and authorize it by the Connection Owner or the Slack member who initiated the target AgentSession. After a channel message is resolved to this Connection and before launch or follow-up, a standalone stop/cancel keyword (after stripping the Bot mention) is treated as a Turn-control request whose authority is decided from recorded input provenance, reusing the existing cancel/stop dispatch.
acceptanceCriteria: The channel ingress detects a standalone stop or cancel keyword in Body.Text after the Bot mention is stripped, using the existing TryGetTurnControlCommand, only after the message is resolved to this Connection (single-mention target or a reply in a thread bound to this Connection), and before any launch or follow-up.

Authority is granted when the sender is the Owner or equals the session initiator resolved via IAgentSessionGrain.GetInitialLaunchAsync().Input.Provenance.MemberId, compared by stable Slack identity; a stop or cancel from any other member is rejected with an actionable reason, creates no resources, and does not interrupt the Turn.

An authorized stop or cancel with an active Turn reuses ResolveCurrentTurnControlAsync and ExecuteTurnControlAsync and returns the existing cancel/stop result kinds; with no active Turn it replies no_active_work or already_ended exactly as the DM path does.
A stop or cancel targets only the Turn active when the request is processed; a gesture for a Turn that has already ended does not stop a later Turn.
A member authorized to invoke the Agent may still send a normal follow-up in a thread bound to a session another member initiated, but their stop or cancel of that session's active Turn is rejected.

Server spec tests cover an Owner stop, a session-initiator stop, rejection of a stop by an allowed non-initiator member with no Turn interruption, an expired gesture not stopping a later Turn, the no-active-work and already-ended replies, and a follow-up still being accepted from an allowed non-initiator; `npm test` passes with fake Slack and injectable time only.
tasks.output: Channel-originated stop and cancel restricted to the Owner or the session initiator, reusing the existing Turn-control dispatch.
tasks.notes: Implements design D5. The initiator is already recorded per accepted input (AgentSessionInputProvenance.MemberId), so authority adds a stable-id compare with no new provenance storage. Depends on T-002 so the 'another allowed member cannot stop another member's Turn' negative case is verifiable with a non-Owner initiator. Does not depend on T-003 (management surface).
